observation: Crude imports recovered close to pre-war run-rate by August as alternative sourcing (Russia/Atlantic Basin) and bypass routes scaled up. Recovery predates the 2026-09-11 Saudi pipeline shutdown.

observation: Steel output fell in Jan-Feb 2026. IMPORTANT: this period is entirely before the war started (2026-02-28); the driver is government capacity-control/anti-involution policy, not the Iran shock. Included only to prevent misattribution.

Cement output fell sharply in March 2026 to the lowest for the period since 2020, driven primarily by the property-sector downturn; energy-cost pass-through from the Iran shock is a secondary, unquantified contributor per the source.
type_supply_or_price_induced: mostly structural (property downturn); partial price-induced margin pressure

observation: Government stood up emergency truck logistics (added ~15000 kl/month capacity from July 2026) to move jet fuel to airports after Hormuz-linked supply-chain disruption affected an estimated 140 flights/week. This is a logistics/distribution bottleneck, not a crude/refining shortfall per se.

East-West Crude Oil Pipeline (1200km, links Gulf fields to Red Sea port of Yanbu) shut after a 2026-09-11 drone attack from Iraq, forcing all rerouted crude back through Hormuz. Saudi refiners report over 90% of Sept-Oct 2026 crude needs already secured, so near-term physical shortfall is expected to be limited. This is a developing event with no realized demand-side macro data yet as of this report as-of date (2026-09-14).
type_supply_or_price_induced: supply-constrained (developing, too recent for demand data)
